messages:
devon: Heads-up — saw a latency spike during the 11:15 load test. P50 up ~2x for small prefix hits. attaching profiler snippets.

karen: ugh. spike when many requests were prefix-hit? details?

devon: yea. cache hit ratio ~62%, but batch sizes collapsed to 1-2 effective tokens. kernel selection kept choosing fp16-kernel-A which is suboptimal for tiny sequences -> per-request overhead dominated. profile excerpt:
```
RPC queue wait: 2ms
kernel setup: 5.8ms
kernel exec: 0.9ms
copy sync: 3ms
```

matt: can you paste the config for the continuous-batcher? maybe threshold too conservative.

devon: current continuous-batcher config:
```
max_tokens_per_batch: 1024
min_batch_accum_time_ms: 2
token_budget_target_percent: 0.6
cache_hit_token_weight: 0.05
```
When many cache hits, effective tokens in batch << expected because we weight hits down; that makes the runtime spin up kernels for tiny real work.

karen: hmmm cache_hit_token_weight seems too small? paradoxically small weight => scheduler assumes more headroom but real compute per request is tiny so we get many tiny kernel launches and wrong kernel selection.

lia: proposal: introduce a 'min_effective_token_budget' floor so even if hits are cheap we aim to accumulate to at least N effective tokens. also tweak kernel selector to incorporate sequence-length variance, not only summed tokens.

devon: ran a quick experiment locally: set min_effective_token_budget=64 and increased cache_hit_token_weight to 0.2. quick load-test numbers: p50 dropped back to baseline, p99 improved slightly. notes:
- avg batch effective tokens: 8 -> 78
- kernel switch ratio to small-seq-optimized kernel: 60% -> 12%
- kernel setup ops/sec: down ~30%

matt: nice. any regressions on latency tail for mixed (cold + cached) workloads?

devon: small bump in cold-start tail (~0.5ms) but overall cost/token down ~4%. profiler shows fewer kernel setups per second which reduces jitter.

karen: can we make this adaptive? during 'rush hour' detect many hits and bump the floor dynamically. maybe use EWMA of avg_effective_tokens with a sliding window.

lia: agree. also add a backpressure rule: if queue_wait_ms > X and avg_batch_effective_tokens < floor -> temporarily raise min_effective_token_budget to avoid floods of tiny batches. that gives us smoothing without hard config flips.

devon: i'll sketch a PR with the adaptive floor + tests and a telemetry patch. cc @ci-bot to run perf job on branch.

ci-bot: perf job queued: build #3425 — will run nightly with synthetic prefix-heavy traces (trace set: prefixed-conv-heavy-v3).

matt: remember to emit tracing tags: batch.effective_tokens, kernel.choice, cache.hit_ratio, batch.accum_time_ms — makes root-cause easier.

karen: also add an alert rule for kernel-switch-rate spikes; we saw ~8k kernel setups/s during the incident which correlates with cost and tail latency.

devon: noted. will open RFC and link perf graphs + flamegraphs. prefer to limit kernel-level changes unless we see persistent inefficiency after batching policy changes. batching first, kernel fallbacks second.

lia: sounds good. if batching policy doesn't fully solve it, we'll loop in kernel owners to add a tiny-seq fast path or change kernel setup amortization.

devon: thanks — i'll post PR link and synthetic run results when ready.
